![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200385/assets/a16176b3fe7ff15ca90aef4a829d53d5f8e64c16c9e0f623ca0d7378cc7fa8f1.png)

The graph of $y={f}^{′}(x)$, the derivative of $y=f(x)$, is defined on the interval $[-3,3]$ as shown above. Find all of the inflection points of $y=f(x)$ for $x\in (-3,3).$
question.worked_solution:
First, note that ${f}^{′}(x)$ exists at every point on the interval $x\in [-3,3].$ 

We need to investigate the behavior of ${f}^{″}(x).$ We recall the following:

- When ${f}^{′}(x)$ is increasing, we have ${f}^{″}(x)>0.$

- When ${f}^{′}(x)$ is decreasing, we have ${f}^{″}(x)<0.$

The function $f(x)$ has an inflection point at $x=a,$ if the following two conditions are satisfied:

- ${f}^{″}(x)=0$ or ${f}^{″}(x)$ is undefined, and

- ${f}^{″}(x)$ changes its sign (from negative to positive or vice versa) at that point.

We summarize the information from the given graph in the table below:

| $x$ | $(-3,-2)$ | $-2$ | $(-2,-1)$ | $-1$ | $(-1,1)$ | $1$ | $(1,3)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}^{′}$ | $↗$ |  | $↘$ |  | $↗$ |  | $↘$ |
| ${f}^{″}$ | $+$ | $0$ | $-$ | $\text{not def.}$ | $+$ | $\text{not def.}$ | $-$ |

From the table, we conclude that ${f}^{″}(x)$ changes its sign at the points $x=-2,$  $x=-1$ and $x=1.$ Therefore, $x=-2,$ $x=-1$ and $x=1$ are  the points of inflection of $y=f(x).$
